create.title: Integer-centred shifted-Gram zero-alias and inverse reduction
create.statement_tex: For one literal flat-smooth strict-UNBAL row R_X=sum_(r odd)chi_4(r)W(X/(rD))sum_k q_L(4Xk/r^2)k^(-1)e(Xk/r), with D=X^delta, L=X^ell, R=X/D and K=XL/D^2, keep every amplitude and the physical denominator 4X frozen at X. For every integer M asymp X, |R_X-R_M^sharp|<<_epsilon(1+|M-X|)X^epsilon. In the shifted length-H block square, the exact ordered-pair kernel Gamma_(M,H)(r,s) is at most a constant times psi_H(M/r)psi_H(M/s)(1+K||M(1/r-1/s)||)^(-A), where psi_H(x)=min(1,(H||x||)^(-1)), and sum_(r asymp R)psi_H(M/r)^2<<_epsilon(1+R/H)X^epsilon. Therefore the complete nearest-alias sector j=0 is O_epsilon((1+R/H)X^epsilon), including every shifted self-correlation and off-diagonal zero alias. At H_0=ceil(X^(1/2)/D)<=K it is square-target-safe. For the unique nearest alias j, with E=M(s-r)-jrs, all nonzero exact aliases E=0 together are O_epsilon(X^epsilon), and |E|>X^(1+rho)/L is rapidly small. Consequently, for every fixed eta>0, any |R_X|>=X^(1/4+eta) forces a positive-real contribution >>X^(1/2+2eta) in the complete signed sector j!=0, E!=0, |E|<=X^(1+eta/10)/L, with both reciprocal selectors, every shifted profile and endpoint, both alias orientations and all character signs retained. This is a one-way fixed-power inverse theorem, not the quarter estimate.
create.next_action: Prove the square-target bound for the complete actual-sign nonzero, nonexact near-alias aggregate at H_0, jointly across transverse modes, shifts, aliases and reciprocal variables. Do not split its conjugate, character, or profile labels before the inequality.

create.title: Unbalanced alias-factor parity and fixed-alias derivative self-return
create.statement_tex: For an integer centre M=2^tM_0 with M_0 odd, the unique reciprocal alias and defect satisfy M(1/r-1/s)=j+E/(rs), (M-jr)(M+js)-M^2=jE, and chi_4(r)chi_4(s)=(-1)^((jrs+E)/2^(t+1)). The factor map is invertible for j!=0 only after retaining its congruences, orientations, supports and literal profiles, and it collapses at j=0. Choosing t with 2^t asymp X^(1/4) is target-safe for the centre perturbation and thins exact aliases, but its near-defect congruence is tautological and removes no original pair. The ordinary same-k Cauchy Gram is a strictly stronger sufficient norm with nondegenerate diagonal R>X^(1/2). In the shifted Gram, transverse Poisson has active modes nu=m-sigma/4 asymp L. The opposite character channel obeys partial_r Phi+m=-(Mh+nu(s^2-r^2))/r^2. For a nonempty alias range there are allowed |h|<H_0 and interior points where this derivative is integral, with second derivative asymp L|j|/X. Therefore neither exact factorization, automatic defect parity, nor a uniform fixed-alias Kusmin-Landau first-derivative bound supplies the missing saving. This is a method obstruction, not a signed lower bound.
create.next_action: Freeze the unshifted positive Gram, automatic two-adic thinning, factorwise absolute values, and fixed-alias first-derivative route. Reopen only with a joint stationary-lattice estimate or a stronger complete-aggregate inverse theorem.

reject.reason: Termwise phase replacement costs up to K. The target-safe result uses the physical product kernel and a divisor layer cake.
Weighted Cauchy is one-way, and the nondegenerate diagonal is R=X/D>X^(1/2). The scalar target need not imply this stronger energy bound.
The positive diagonal belongs to a stronger sufficient norm. Its cancellation burden is not a lower bound for the original scalar row.
A tie would give 2M(s-r)=(2j+1)rs, impossible because the left side is even and the right side is odd.
The divisor factorization uv=M^2 controls only E=0. The live window has 0<|E|<=X^(1+rho)/L and retains every factor congruence and profile.
The displayed parity quotient equals M_0(s-r)/2 and is exactly the original chi_4(r)chi_4(s) sign under the inverse map.
Swapping r and s conjugates the analytic kernel but leaves the character product unchanged. The two orientations combine as a real part, not automatic cancellation.
It forces a large modulus only on exact aliases, which are already divisor-small. Every original near pair defines a defect satisfying the new congruence.

The exact block-square kernel has two reciprocal selectors. A product layer cake proves the complete j=0 sector, including all shifted self-correlations and off-diagonal zero aliases, is target-safe at H_0.
Multiplying nominal densities proves neither an arithmetic upper bound nor a lower-bound obstruction for the correlated thin annulus.
All transverse modes nu=m-sigma/4 asymp L are active, and allowed h-shifts create nondegenerate interior derivative crossings in the opposite character channel.
The nonzero, nonexact near-alias aggregate and every nonflat owner remain open.

round_assessment.reason: Round 123 proves target-safe movable-centre stability, exact alias-factor algebra, a complete shifted zero-alias theorem, global exact-alias and far-tail deletions, and a fixed-power inverse reduction to one explicit actual-sign near-alias aggregate. It also rigorously rules out automatic two-adic thinning and the proposed fixed-alias first-derivative shortcut. The complete flat-smooth target, every nonflat M2 owner, all M1 parents and every exponent remain open.
